about: AI crawlers and robots.txt tokens, from each vendor's own page. Re-read every page at each release and at least once a month; a row whose page could not be read gets "verified": false, and no counted or scored check may rest on it. role: search = builds an index for AI answers; mixed = a search engine crawler whose index also feeds AI features; training = collects content for model training; control = a robots.txt token that only states a preference, no crawler uses it; user = fetches a page when a person asks; policy = a shared preference token. robots, only what the vendor's page states: obeys = the vendor says the crawler follows (respects, obeys) robots.txt; documented = the vendor documents a robots.txt setting for it (what a disallow does, or that robots.txt tags manage it) without saying it always follows robots.txt; may_ignore = the vendor says robots.txt may not apply; ignores = the vendor says it generally ignores robots.txt. counted = one of the AI search crawlers the ai module counts.

bots.product: ChatGPT search
bots.says: OpenAI's robots.txt tags let sites manage it; a site opted out of it is not shown in ChatGPT search answers, though it can still appear as a navigational link.

bots.product: Claude search
bots.says: Anthropic says its bots honour robots.txt; disabling Claude-SearchBot prevents indexing for search, which may reduce the site's visibility and accuracy in user search results.

bots.product: Perplexity search
bots.says: Perplexity says webmasters can use its robots.txt tags to manage how their sites interact with Perplexity, and recommends allowing PerplexityBot; it surfaces sites in Perplexity's search results and is not used for AI foundation models.

bots.product: Bing search (Bing's webmaster guidelines say Copilot rests on the same crawling and index)
bots.says: Bing's standard crawler; Microsoft says robots.txt files can be configured to tell Bing's crawlers how to interact with a site. Its crawler page lists no separate crawler for AI features.
bots.training_control: From 2027-02-01 Bing reads the shared __usage_ai-training group and, per page, <meta name="Bingbot" content="ai-training:disallow">.

bots.product: Siri, Spotlight and Safari suggestions; context for Apple's AI features
bots.says: Apple says Applebot respects standard robots.txt directives in general search crawls aimed at it, and does not follow crawl-delay; when robots.txt does not mention Applebot but mentions Googlebot, it follows the Googlebot instructions.
bots.training_control: Disallow Applebot-Extended to keep content out of Apple's model training; the page stays in Apple's search features.

bots.product: DuckDuckGo AI-assisted answers
bots.says: DuckDuckGo says that once robots.txt disallows DuckAssistBot, the change takes effect after 72 hours and it stops crawling the site, without changing organic rankings; the data is not used to train models.

bots.product: Google Search
bots.says: Google says its common crawlers, Googlebot among them, always obey robots.txt rules when crawling automatically. The seo module checks it.

bots.product: Meta AI search
bots.says: Meta says robots.txt lets a site specify how its crawlers interact with it; allowing Meta-WebIndexer helps Meta cite and link the site in Meta AI's responses.

bots.product: Mistral search
bots.says: Mistral uses specific robots.txt tags for its crawlers; this one crawls only to index content for Mistral search and is not used for training.

bots.product: Search in Amazon products such as Alexa
bots.says: Amazon says its automated crawling respects the Robots Exclusion Protocol; allowing it makes content eligible for Amazon's search. When robots.txt does not name it, Amazon says it follows the rules given to other search bots, which Seekwide does not model.

bots.product: Training OpenAI's foundation models
bots.says: Disallowing GPTBot indicates the site's content should not be used to train OpenAI's generative AI foundation models.

bots.product: Training Anthropic's models
bots.says: Anthropic says its bots honour robots.txt; disallowing ClaudeBot signals that the site's future content should be excluded from Anthropic's training datasets, and a rule that names ClaudeBot takes priority over the shared training preference.

bots.product: The Common Crawl dataset, used to train many models
bots.says: Common Crawl documents a CCBot group with Disallow: / to stop it from crawling the site.

bots.product: Training Meta's foundation models and indexing
bots.says: Meta says robots.txt lets a site specify how its crawlers interact with it; this one crawls for uses such as training foundation AI models or improving products by indexing content directly.

bots.product: Training Mistral's models
bots.says: Mistral says webmasters can disallow this user agent in robots.txt; it builds datasets for training Mistral's models.

bots.product: Amazon products; may train Amazon's AI models
bots.says: Amazon says its automated crawling respects the Robots Exclusion Protocol; Amazonbot improves Amazon's products and services and may be used to train Amazon's AI models.

bots.product: Gemini training and grounding; no crawler of its own
bots.says: A standalone product token, not a crawler, to manage whether content may be used for Gemini training and grounding; it does not affect inclusion in Google Search and is not a ranking signal.

bots.product: Training Apple's foundation models; no crawler of its own
bots.says: Disallowing Applebot-Extended in robots.txt opts content out of training Apple's generative foundation models; such pages can still be included in Apple's search results.

bots.product: Pages ChatGPT opens when a user asks
bots.says: Because a user starts these requests, robots.txt rules may not apply; it does not decide what appears in ChatGPT search.

bots.product: Pages Claude opens when a user asks
bots.says: Disallowing it stops Claude from retrieving the site's content in answer to a user's question.

bots.product: Pages Perplexity opens when a user asks
bots.says: Because a user requested the fetch, it generally ignores robots.txt rules.

bots.product: Pages Mistral's Vibe opens when a user asks
bots.says: Mistral says the MistralAI-User robots.txt token governs which sites these user requests can be made to.

bots.product: Agents on Google's infrastructure acting for a user
bots.says: A user-triggered fetcher; Google says such fetchers generally ignore robots.txt rules.

bots.product: Links Meta's AI fetches when a user asks
bots.says: Fetches links at a user's request and may bypass robots.txt rules.

bots.product: Pages Alexa opens when a user asks
bots.says: Because a user can start its actions, it may not follow all robots.txt rules.

bots.product: A shared no-training preference (individual IETF draft)
bots.says: A User-Agent group for this token states a training preference; a User-Agent: * group never applies to it.
